name: Auction house
description: Collectors with private valuations bid for three identical vases. The same crowd meets every auction format as an experiment arm: sealed first-price (base), Vickrey second-price, English, Dutch, uniform-price and a double auction against dealers.

brief.situation: An auction house sells antique vases. Every collector has a private idea of what one vase is worth to them.
brief.rules: Bid for vases with the auction tool; how bids win and what the winner pays depends on the auction format described with each lot. Money for a bid is held until the lot closes, and you get back whatever you do not pay. Your score is the value of the vases you win minus what you paid.

value.description: What one vase is worth to this collector.

dealer.description: A dealer holding vases; trades only in the double auction.

cost.description: What a vase cost the dealer.

population.name: Collector {$i}
population.brief: A vase is worth {$actor.value|money} to you.

population.brief: Each of your vases cost you {$actor.cost|money}.

first_price.description: Sealed first-price: the highest bid wins and pays its bid.

second_price.description: Sealed Vickrey: the highest bid wins and pays the second-highest.

english.description: Open ascending bids with a $5 increment.

dutch.description: A clock falling $15 a round from $170.

uniform.description: All three vases in one lot at one clearing price.

double.description: Dealers ask, collectors bid, cleared together each round.

surplus.description: Collectors' value won minus what they paid.

allocated_value.description: Total value of the vases to whoever won them.
